ask/read: A language model reads “the capital of Italy is”, and has to guess the next word. Follow the last word up through the model: its vector, the residual stream, rises past one block after another.
ask/top: Only at the very top does the model answer. The unembedding, W U, gives every token a score, its logit, and Rome's is the highest.
ask/ask: In between, the stream is just a list of numbers, with no labels on them. So ask a simpler question: if the model stopped halfway up, what would it say?
ask/same: The stream halfway up is the same kind of vector as at the top: x zero plus the writes so far, just as wide. Only the later blocks' writes are missing.
ask/lens: So read it with the same W U. Do that at every height, and you see the model's guess so far, block by block.
ask/name: This is the logit lens. Logit, because what it reads out is logits. A lens, because it is a way of looking inside the model.
ask/borrow: Nothing new is trained: the lens borrows the model's own W U, just as it is.
ask/history: A writer known online as nostalgebraist named it, in a 2020 post about G P T two, a model with forty-eight blocks. Read after its twelfth block, or its thirty-third, the stream already made sense as a guess.
ask/forms: The early guesses were generally wrong, but often sensible in some way, and they sharpened, block by block, toward the final answer. Here: a capital, then a city in Italy, then Rome.
example/setup: Now with numbers. A tiny model reads the same words. Its stream is two numbers wide, and three tokens matter: Paris, Milan and Rome. Here is each one's row of W U.
example/x0: At the bottom, the stream is x zero: one, zero.
example/dot: Paris's row is two, zero. Dotted with the stream: two times one, plus zero times zero, makes two.
example/rest: Milan scores one, and Rome zero. So at the bottom, the lens says Paris: a capital, but the wrong one.
example/write: Block zero writes minus one, two. Added in, the stream becomes zero, two.
example/again: Read it again with the same rows. Now Paris scores zero, Milan two, and Rome four. After block zero, the lens says Rome.
example/later: Every write still to come can change which token is on top. So a lens partway up shows the prediction so far, and only so far.
